# Untying Prefill and Decode Loops in Looped Language Models

> Looped (recurrent-depth) language models run one block of layers several times per token and, at inference, run the
> same number of loops to prefill the prompt and to decode each answer token. This work unties the two with a small
> loop adapter (LoRA + per-loop RoPE-commuting KV maps on a frozen model; one set of parameters for all 16 pairs of
> prefill loops m and decode loops n up to four) and measures what each count buys on Ouro-2.6B, Ouro-1.4B,
> Ouro-2.6B-Thinking, Ouro-1.4B-Thinking, SenseNova-Loop-9B-Preview and Lev looped decision models. The paper's statistics
> are recomputed from released per-item scores by ouro/scripts/paper_numbers.py.

Main findings (95% paired bootstrap intervals in the paper; Ouro's own evaluation protocol):
- Prefill with more loops than you decode: with one decode loop the best prefill count is 2-4 on all 15 benchmark
  settings of the Ouro-2.6B task map, never 1.
- Choosing m per benchmark on held-out halves beats native Ouro-2.6B 1/1 significantly on 14 of 15 settings (+3.9 to
  +21.3), the same adapter at prefill 1 on 10, and a LoRA-distilled native 1/1 (same data and teacher) on 9; at two
  decode loops distillation matches it, at three or four the native model is as good. Ouro-1.4B: 13 and 3 of 15.
- Ouro-2.6B-Thinking: prefill 4 / decode 2 above native 2/2 on all eight benchmarks (significant on four), above a
  distilled 2/2 on MMLU-Pro (+6.0) and ARC-C (+3.2); 0.59x the answer time of native 4/4 on 192 timed GSM8K problems.
- Lev looped decision models, both directions: more prefill than decision loops is significantly above a matched
  control on 12 of 13 (m, n) pairs; fewer is below it on all 13 (significantly 11), in each of four seeds.
- One stored prompt KV cache serves every decode loop exactly (RoPE-commuting key scale applied to the query).

Limitations stated by the author: the prefill count is calibrated per benchmark, not routed per prompt; the advantage is largest at one decode loop
(at two, distillation matches it on the base model); with three or four decode loops native models are as good or better; comparisons with native models include adapter training; equal decode loops do not mean equal latency.

## Docs
- README.md: findings, when to use, repository map
- REPRODUCE.md: every table and figure -> script -> result file; training and evaluation commands
- paper/untying-prefill-decode-loops.pdf: the paper
- ouro/results/items/: per-item scores of every run the paper uses; ouro/results/paper_numbers.json: the recomputed statistics
